data.name: Kisun
data.gender_notes: Kisun is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Surya', meaning 'Sun'. In Hindu mythology, Kisun is a name for the sun god. The name Kisun carries the meaning “Sun God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kisun usually hope their child will grow to embody sun god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Bringer of light and warmth, a symbol of divine power.
data.etymology: Kisun belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sun God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kisun total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kisun holds a significant cultural significance as it is derived from the Sanskrit word for the sun god. In Hindu culture, the sun is revered as a symbol of strength, energy, and life-givingforce.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Kisun represents the divine power of the sun god, who is believed to provide light, warmth, and energy to the world. It signifies that the individual named Kisun is a divine child of the sun, bestowed with the strength, courage, and vitality of the sun. This name is a powerful reminder of the transformative power of the sun, and the divine connection between the individual and the cosmos.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Kisun is derived from the Sanskrit word "Kishor," meaning youthful, vibrant, and full of energy. It symbolizes the spirit of new beginnings, growth, and vitality in one's life. The name is believed to bestow upon its bearer the strength and enthusiasm to overcome challenges and thrive in all endeavors.

historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata mentions a king named Kisura, who was the king of Kalinga during the great battle of Kurukshetra.
Another reference to King Kisuka, who ruled the Vangala country (modern day Andhra Pradesh) in the 2nd century BCE, is found in the Jataka tales.
